lines: He are my brother.

why.en: A single he/she subject takes the singular form of 'be'.
why.ko: 주어가 he 한 사람 → be동사도 단수형.

gloss.en: He is my brother.

lines: I is not ready yet.

why.en: The subject 'I' has its own form of 'be'.
why.ko: 주어 I는 be동사 꼴이 따로 정해져 있다.

gloss.en: I am not ready yet.

lines: The keys is in my bag.

why.en: 'Keys' is plural, so 'be' must be plural too.
why.ko: keys는 여러 개 → be동사도 복수형.

gloss.en: The keys are in my bag.

lines: My boss are very strict.

why.en: One boss is a singular subject.
why.ko: 상사 한 사람 → 단수 주어.

gloss.en: My boss is very strict.

lines: She live in Seoul.

why.en: In the present simple, he/she/it verbs end in -s.
why.ko: 현재시제에서 he/she/it 주어면 동사에 -s.

gloss.en: She lives in Seoul.

lines: She work hard every day.

why.en: A she-subject in the present simple needs the -s ending.
why.ko: 현재시제 she 주어 → 동사 끝에 -s.

gloss.en: She works hard every day.

lines: He walk to school every day.

why.en: Habits of 'he' in the present simple take -s.
why.ko: he의 습관을 말하는 현재시제 → 동사에 -s.

gloss.en: He walks to school every day.

lines: She water her garden every morning.

why.en: With 'she', the present-simple verb ends in -s.
why.ko: she 주어 현재시제 → 동사에 -s.

gloss.en: She waters her garden every morning.
gloss.ko: 그녀는 매일 아침 정원에 물을 줘.

lines: That's an great idea for the party!

why.en: 'Great' starts with a consonant sound, so the short article is used.
why.ko: great는 자음 소리로 시작 → 짧은 관사.

gloss.en: That's a great idea for the party!

lines: She is an member of the club.

why.en: Before a consonant sound like 'm', the article has no -n.
why.ko: m 같은 자음 소리 앞에서는 n 없는 관사.

gloss.en: She is a member of the club.

lines: I'll call you in a hour.

why.en: The 'h' in 'hour' is silent, so the word starts with a vowel sound.
why.ko: hour의 h는 소리 나지 않음 → 모음 소리로 시작.

gloss.en: I'll call you in an hour.

lines: I have two sister.

why.en: After 'two', the noun must be plural.
why.ko: two 뒤의 명사는 복수형.

gloss.en: I have two sisters.

lines: There are seven day in a week.

why.en: 'Seven' counts more than one, so the noun takes -s.
why.ko: seven은 여럿 → 명사에 -s.

gloss.en: There are seven days in a week.

lines: We need three chair for this table.

why.en: Three of something means a plural noun.
why.ko: 세 개 → 복수 명사.

gloss.en: We need three chairs for this table.
gloss.ko: 이 탁자에 의자 세 개가 필요해.

lines: She borrowed three book from the library.

why.en: A number above one needs a plural noun.
why.ko: 하나보다 많은 수 → 복수 명사.

gloss.en: She borrowed three books from the library.
gloss.ko: 그녀는 도서관에서 책 세 권을 빌렸어.

lines: Does she likes apples?

why.en: After 'does', the main verb goes back to its base form.
why.ko: does 뒤의 동사는 원형.

gloss.en: Does she like apples?

lines: Does you know her name?

why.en: Questions with 'you' use the helper without -es.
why.ko: you 의문문은 -es 없는 조동사.

gloss.en: Do you know her name?

lines: Do your sister like coffee?

why.en: 'Your sister' is a she-subject, so the helper takes -es.
why.ko: your sister는 she 주어 → 조동사에 -es.

gloss.en: Does your sister like coffee?

lines: I don't drinks coffee at night.

why.en: After don't/doesn't, the verb stays in its base form.
why.ko: don't 뒤의 동사는 원형.

gloss.en: I don't drink coffee at night.

lines: I like to read in night.

why.en: 'Night' on its own takes the point-in-time preposition.
why.ko: night 단독은 '시점' 전치사와 쓴다.

gloss.en: I like to read at night.
gloss.ko: 나는 밤에 책 읽는 걸 좋아해.

lines: My birthday is on September.

why.en: Months take the same preposition as years and seasons, not the one for days.
why.ko: 달(월)은 날짜·요일과 다른 전치사 — 해·계절과 같은 것.

gloss.en: My birthday is in September.

lines: The leaves fall on autumn.

why.en: Seasons take the 'inside a period' preposition.
why.ko: 계절은 '기간 안' 전치사.

gloss.en: The leaves fall in autumn.

lines: I wake up on six every day.

why.en: Clock times take the point-in-time preposition; the day one is for dates and weekdays.
why.ko: 시각은 '시점' 전치사 — 요일·날짜용이 아니다.

gloss.en: I wake up at six every day.

lines: Can you drives a car?

why.en: After 'can', the verb is always in its base form.
why.ko: can 뒤의 동사는 늘 원형.

gloss.en: Can you drive a car?

lines: She can sings very well.

why.en: 'Can' never adds -s to the verb after it, even with 'she'.
why.ko: can 뒤 동사는 she여도 -s가 붙지 않는다.

gloss.en: She can sing very well.

lines: I can't reaching the top shelf.

why.en: After can/can't, use the plain verb, not the -ing form.
why.ko: can't 뒤에는 -ing가 아니라 원형.

gloss.en: I can't reach the top shelf.
gloss.ko: 맨 위 선반에 손이 안 닿아.

lines: I meet him a year ago.

why.en: 'A year ago' is finished past time, so the verb must be past.
why.ko: a year ago는 끝난 과거 → 동사도 과거형.

gloss.en: I met him a year ago.

lines: She finded a new job last week.

why.en: 'Find' is irregular; its past form doesn't add -ed.
why.ko: find는 불규칙 동사 — 과거형에 -ed를 붙이지 않는다.

gloss.en: She found a new job last week.

lines: I catched a cold last week.

why.en: 'Catch' has an irregular past form.
why.ko: catch는 과거형이 불규칙.

gloss.en: I caught a cold last week.

lines: We watch a movie last night.

why.en: 'Last night' is over, so the verb needs the past -ed.
why.ko: last night은 지난 일 → 동사에 과거 -ed.

gloss.en: We watched a movie last night.

lines: They are play soccer.

why.en: An action happening now is 'be' + verb-ing.
why.ko: 지금 하는 일 = be + 동사-ing.

gloss.en: They are playing soccer.

lines: The baby is sleep in the crib.

why.en: After 'is' for an action in progress, the verb takes -ing.
why.ko: 진행 중인 일 is 뒤 → 동사-ing.

gloss.en: The baby is sleeping in the crib.

lines: She is cooks dinner in the kitchen.

why.en: 'Is' + a verb for something happening now needs the -ing form.
why.ko: 지금 하는 일 is + 동사 → -ing 꼴.

gloss.en: She is cooking dinner in the kitchen.

lines: I will calling you later.

why.en: 'Will' is followed by the plain verb.
why.ko: will 뒤에는 동사 원형.

gloss.en: I will call you later.

lines: I will arrived at noon.

why.en: After 'will', the verb has no past ending.
why.ko: will 뒤 동사에는 과거 꼬리가 붙지 않는다.

gloss.en: I will arrive at noon.

lines: I will sent the package tomorrow.

why.en: A future plan with 'will' uses the base verb, not the past.
why.ko: will로 말하는 앞일 → 과거형이 아닌 원형.

gloss.en: I will send the package tomorrow.

lines: He is tall than his brother.

why.en: 'Than' needs the comparative (-er) form of the adjective.
why.ko: than 앞 형용사는 비교급(-er).

gloss.en: He is taller than his brother.

lines: My mom makes the goodest soup.

why.en: 'Good' has an irregular superlative.
why.ko: good의 최상급은 불규칙.

gloss.en: My mom makes the best soup.

lines: Good health is most important than money.

why.en: Comparing two things with 'than' uses the comparative, not the superlative.
why.ko: than으로 둘을 비교 → 최상급이 아니라 비교급.

gloss.en: Good health is more important than money.

lines: I don't have many time.

why.en: 'Time' here is uncountable, so it can't take the word for countable nouns.
why.ko: 여기서 time은 셀 수 없는 명사 → 셀 수 있는 명사용 낱말은 못 씀.

gloss.en: I don't have much time.

lines: There are much shops around here.

why.en: 'Shops' is a countable plural noun.
why.ko: shops는 셀 수 있는 복수 명사.

gloss.en: There are many shops around here.

lines: I have too many stuff in my room.

why.en: 'Stuff' is uncountable.
why.ko: stuff는 셀 수 없는 명사.

gloss.en: I have too much stuff in my room.

lines: Is this bag your?

why.en: With no noun after it, the possessive must be the pronoun form.
why.ko: 뒤에 명사가 없으면 소유대명사 꼴.

gloss.en: Is this bag yours?

lines: That car is our.

why.en: At the end of the sentence with no noun, use the possessive pronoun.
why.ko: 문장 끝, 뒤에 명사 없음 → 소유대명사.

gloss.en: That car is ours.

lines: They brought their dog with they.

why.en: After a preposition like 'with', a pronoun takes its object form.
why.ko: with 같은 전치사 뒤 대명사는 목적격.

gloss.en: They brought their dog with them.

lines: She has live here for one year.

why.en: The present perfect is have/has + past participle.
why.ko: 현재완료 = have/has + 과거분사.

gloss.en: She has lived here for one year.

lines: I have see that movie twice.

why.en: After 'have' in the present perfect, use the past participle.
why.ko: 현재완료 have 뒤에는 과거분사.

gloss.en: I have seen that movie twice.
gloss.ko: 나는 그 영화를 두 번 봤어.

lines: I has seen this movie before.

why.en: With 'I', the present perfect helper has no -s.
why.ko: I 주어 현재완료 조동사에는 -s가 없다.

gloss.en: I have seen this movie before.
gloss.ko: 이 영화 전에 본 적 있어.

lines: A monster was hide under the bed.

why.en: The past continuous is was/were + verb-ing.
why.ko: 과거진행 = was/were + 동사-ing.

gloss.en: A monster was hiding under the bed.

lines: Kids was playing in the fountain in the plaza.

why.en: 'Kids' is plural, so the past of 'be' must be plural.
why.ko: kids는 복수 → be 과거형도 복수.

gloss.en: Kids were playing in the fountain in the plaza.

lines: If you drop the glass, it will shattered.

why.en: In the result part, 'will' takes the base verb.
why.ko: 결과 쪽 will 뒤에는 동사 원형.

gloss.en: If you drop the glass, it will shatter.

lines: He had to yelled to be heard over the noise.

why.en: 'Had to' already shows the past; the verb after it stays in base form.
why.ko: had to가 이미 과거 → 뒤 동사는 원형.

gloss.en: He had to yell to be heard over the noise.
gloss.ko: 그는 소음 속에서도 들리게 소리를 질러야 했어.

lines: They had to cancelled the meeting.

why.en: After 'had to', the verb is not marked for past again.
why.ko: had to 뒤 동사에 과거 표시를 또 하지 않는다.

gloss.en: They had to cancel the meeting.

lines: You should applying for the job soon.

why.en: 'Should' is followed by the base verb.
why.ko: should 뒤에는 동사 원형.

gloss.en: You should apply for the job soon.
gloss.ko: 그 일자리에 빨리 지원하는 게 좋겠어.

lines: I look forward to see you soon.

why.en: In 'look forward to', 'to' is a preposition, so the verb takes -ing.
why.ko: look forward to의 to는 전치사 → 동사는 -ing.

gloss.en: I look forward to seeing you soon.

lines: I enjoy spend time with my family.

why.en: 'Enjoy' is followed by the -ing form.
why.ko: enjoy 뒤에는 -ing.

gloss.en: I enjoy spending time with my family.
gloss.ko: 나는 가족과 시간을 보내는 게 즐거워.

lines: I hope to seeing you soon.

why.en: 'Hope to' is followed by the base verb.
why.ko: hope to 뒤에는 동사 원형.

gloss.en: I hope to see you soon.

lines: I met a girl who smile was beautiful.

why.en: The smile belongs to the girl, so the relative word must show possession.
why.ko: 미소는 그 소녀의 것 → 소유를 나타내는 관계사.

gloss.en: I met a girl whose smile was beautiful.

lines: He is a former athlete which now coaches kids.

why.en: An athlete is a person, so the relative pronoun must be the one for people.
why.ko: 운동선수는 사람 → 사람용 관계대명사.

gloss.en: He is a former athlete who now coaches kids.
gloss.ko: 그는 지금 아이들을 가르치는 전직 운동선수야.

lines: She is a versatile musician who play many instruments.

why.en: 'Who' refers to one musician, so the verb is singular.
why.ko: who는 음악가 한 사람 → 동사도 단수.

gloss.en: She is a versatile musician who plays many instruments.
gloss.ko: 그녀는 여러 악기를 연주하는 다재다능한 음악가야.

lines: The window is make of glass.

why.en: The passive is 'be' + past participle.
why.ko: 수동태 = be + 과거분사.

gloss.en: The window is made of glass.

lines: The national flag was rose at the ceremony.

why.en: Someone lifted the flag, so you need the passive of the verb that takes an object.
why.ko: 누군가 깃발을 올림 → 목적어를 받는 동사의 수동태.

gloss.en: The national flag was raised at the ceremony.

lines: True friendship is build on trust.

why.en: After 'is' in a passive, use the past participle.
why.ko: 수동태 is 뒤에는 과거분사.

gloss.en: True friendship is built on trust.

lines: The lecture was such boring that I almost slept.

why.en: Before an adjective with no noun, use the word that goes with adjectives alone.
why.ko: 명사 없이 형용사만 오면 형용사 앞에 쓰는 말.

gloss.en: The lecture was so boring that I almost slept.
gloss.ko: 강의가 너무 지루해서 거의 잠들 뻔했어.

lines: The hill was such steep that we had to climb slowly.

why.en: 'Steep' is an adjective with no noun after it.
why.ko: steep 뒤에 명사가 없다 → 형용사용 말.

gloss.en: The hill was so steep that we had to climb slowly.
gloss.ko: 언덕이 너무 가팔라서 천천히 올라가야 했어.

lines: I complete agree with you.

why.en: A word describing the verb 'agree' must be an adverb.
why.ko: 동사 agree를 꾸미는 말 → 부사.

gloss.en: I completely agree with you.

lines: Her health has improved significant.

why.en: To describe how something improved, use an adverb.
why.ko: 어떻게 좋아졌는지 → 부사.

gloss.en: Her health has improved significantly.

lines: If you persist, you will success.

why.en: After 'will', you need a verb, not a noun.
why.ko: will 뒤에는 명사가 아니라 동사.

gloss.en: If you persist, you will succeed.

lines: Please fill on this form.

why.en: Completing a form uses a fixed phrasal verb with a different particle.
why.ko: 양식을 채우는 것은 정해진 구동사 — 다른 부사.

gloss.en: Please fill out this form.

lines: My blue pen ran off of ink.

why.en: Having none left is a fixed phrasal verb: run ___ of.
why.ko: 다 떨어짐은 정해진 구동사 run ___ of.

gloss.en: My blue pen ran out of ink.

lines: I did a mistake on my test.

why.en: 'Mistake' collocates with a different verb than 'do'.
why.ko: mistake와 짝이 되는 동사는 do가 아니다.

gloss.en: I made a mistake on my test.

lines: I do a shower every morning.

why.en: 'Shower' doesn't pair with 'do'; English uses the verb you'd use for a nap or a break.
why.ko: shower는 do와 짝이 아니다 — nap·break(쉬다)와 같은 동사를 쓴다.

gloss.en: I take a shower every morning.

lines: Doing a decision can be hard.

why.en: 'Decision' collocates with the same verb as 'mistake'.
why.ko: decision은 mistake와 같은 동사와 짝.

gloss.en: Making a decision can be hard.
gloss.ko: 결정을 내리는 건 어려울 수 있어.

lines: Please make attention to the teacher.

why.en: 'Attention' pairs with the verb used for bills and compliments, not 'make'.
why.ko: attention은 make가 아니라 bill(요금)·compliment(칭찬)와 같은 동사와 짝.

gloss.en: Please pay attention to the teacher.

lines: There was strong rain all night long.

why.en: A lot of rain is described with a weight word, not a power word.
why.ko: 비가 많이 오면 '힘'이 아니라 '무게' 말로.

gloss.en: There was heavy rain all night long.

lines: I need to make my laundry this afternoon.

why.en: Household chores like laundry use the same verb as 'homework' and 'the dishes'.
why.ko: 빨래 같은 집안일은 homework·the dishes와 같은 동사.

gloss.en: I need to do my laundry this afternoon.

lines: She makes research on climate change.

why.en: 'Research' collocates with the same verb as homework.
why.ko: research는 homework와 같은 동사와 짝.

gloss.en: She does research on climate change.

lines: Talking to a therapist can really do a difference.

why.en: The fixed phrase for having an effect is '___ a difference'.
why.ko: 효과가 있다는 고정 표현 '___ a difference'.

gloss.en: Talking to a therapist can really make a difference.
gloss.ko: 상담사와 이야기하는 게 정말 도움이 될 수 있어.

lines: In additional, I want to thank everyone.

why.en: After 'In', the linker needs a noun, not an adjective.
why.ko: In 뒤 연결어는 형용사가 아니라 명사.

gloss.en: In addition, I want to thank everyone.

lines: I wish I can sing well.

why.en: A wish about the present moves the verb one step into the past.
why.ko: 지금에 대한 바람은 동사를 한 단계 과거로.

gloss.en: I wish I could sing well.

lines: I will go if I had time.

why.en: 'Had' in the if-part marks an unreal situation, so the result can't be a real future.
why.ko: if 쪽 had = 사실이 아닌 상황 → 결과도 실제 미래가 아니다.

gloss.en: I would go if I had time.

lines: Although the rain, we went for a walk.

why.en: 'The rain' is a noun phrase with no verb, so a conjunction can't introduce it.
why.ko: the rain은 동사 없는 명사구 → 접속사로 이을 수 없다.

gloss.en: Despite the rain, we went for a walk.

lines: Despite he was tired, he finished his homework.

why.en: A full clause with a verb follows, so you need a conjunction, not a preposition.
why.ko: 뒤에 동사 있는 절 → 전치사가 아니라 접속사.

gloss.en: Although he was tired, he finished his homework.

lines: Although his success, he remains humble.

why.en: 'His success' is a noun phrase, so it needs a preposition.
why.ko: his success는 명사구 → 전치사가 필요.

gloss.en: Despite his success, he remains humble.

lines: The complete of the project took two years.

why.en: Between 'The' and 'of', the word must be a noun.
why.ko: The와 of 사이에는 명사.

gloss.en: The completion of the project took two years.

lines: The introduce of the new law changed everything.

why.en: After 'The', a verb must become its noun form.
why.ko: The 뒤에서 동사는 명사 꼴로.

gloss.en: The introduction of the new law changed everything.
gloss.ko: 새 법의 도입이 모든 것을 바꿨어.

lines: His lacking of confidence surprised me.

why.en: After 'His' and before 'of', the plain noun is needed.
why.ko: His 뒤, of 앞에는 그냥 명사.

gloss.en: His lack of confidence surprised me.
gloss.ko: 그의 자신감 부족이 나를 놀라게 했어.

lines: Prices tend to increasing every year.

why.en: 'Tend to' is followed by the base verb.
why.ko: tend to 뒤에는 동사 원형.

gloss.en: Prices tend to increase every year.

lines: I am not entire sure about the answer.

why.en: Softening 'sure' needs an adverb, not an adjective.
why.ko: sure를 누그러뜨리는 말은 형용사가 아니라 부사.

gloss.en: I am not entirely sure about the answer.
gloss.ko: 그 답에 대해 완전히 확신하진 않아.

lines: To some extend, I agree with you.

why.en: The phrase needs the noun (degree), not the verb meaning 'stretch'.
why.ko: 여기엔 '정도'라는 명사 — '늘리다' 동사가 아니다.

gloss.en: To some extent, I agree with you.

lines: I forgot my umbrella, so I got dry in the rain.

why.en: No umbrella in the rain → you would end up soaked.
why.ko: 우산 없이 비를 맞음 → 젖었을 것.

gloss.en: I forgot my umbrella, so I got wet in the rain.

lines: You deserve a break after working so little.

why.en: You earn a break by working a lot, not barely working.
why.ko: 쉴 자격은 많이 일해야 생긴다.

gloss.en: You deserve a break after working so hard.
gloss.ko: 그렇게 열심히 일했으니 쉴 자격이 있어.

lines: I'm too strong to lift this box.

why.en: 'Too … to lift' means lacking strength.
why.ko: '너무 …해서 못 든다' → 힘이 없다는 뜻.

gloss.en: I'm too weak to lift this box.
gloss.ko: 나는 힘이 없어서 이 상자를 못 들어.

lines: This steak is too tender to eat.

why.en: Meat you can't eat is hard to chew, not soft.
why.ko: 먹을 수 없는 고기 → 부드러운 게 아니라 질기다.

gloss.en: This steak is too tough to eat.
gloss.ko: 이 스테이크는 너무 질겨서 못 먹겠어.

lines: He is weak enough to lift it alone.

why.en: Lifting it alone takes power.
why.ko: 혼자 드는 데는 힘이 필요하다.

gloss.en: He is strong enough to lift it alone.
gloss.ko: 그는 혼자 그걸 들 만큼 힘이 세.

lines: We held a physical meeting instead of meeting in person.

why.en: 'Instead of meeting in person' means the meeting was online.
why.ko: '직접 만나는 대신' → 온라인 회의였다.

gloss.en: We held a virtual meeting instead of meeting in person.
gloss.ko: 우리는 직접 만나는 대신 화상 회의를 했어.

lines: I forgot my pen, so I need to lend one.

why.en: Without your own pen, you need to get one from someone.
why.ko: 펜이 없으면 남에게서 받아야 한다.

gloss.en: I forgot my pen, so I need to borrow one.

lines: Lower your hand if you know the answer.

why.en: To show you know the answer, you put your hand up.
why.ko: 답을 안다고 알리려면 손을 든다.

gloss.en: Raise your hand if you know the answer.

lines: There is a café nearby if you get full.

why.en: A café is useful when you want food.
why.ko: 카페는 먹을 게 필요할 때 쓸모 있다.

gloss.en: There is a café nearby if you get hungry.

lines: Check your temperature if you feel well.

why.en: You check your temperature when something feels wrong.
why.ko: 몸이 이상할 때 체온을 잰다.

gloss.en: Check your temperature if you feel sick.

lines: It's harmful to ask questions if you’re confused.

why.en: Asking questions when confused makes things clearer.
why.ko: 헷갈릴 때 묻는 건 이해에 보탬이 된다.

gloss.en: It's helpful to ask questions if you’re confused.

lines: We had to continue the game because of rain.

why.en: Rain forces a game to stop, not to go on.
why.ko: 비 때문에 해야 했던 일 → 경기를 멈춤.

gloss.en: We had to suspend the game because of rain.

lines: You should celebrate if you hurt someone’s feelings.

why.en: Hurting someone calls for saying sorry.
why.ko: 남의 마음을 다치게 했으면 사과해야 한다.

gloss.en: You should apologize if you hurt someone’s feelings.
gloss.ko: 누군가의 마음을 다치게 했다면 사과해야 해.

lines: The balloon might shrink if you keep blowing.

why.en: Blowing more air in makes a balloon bigger until it bursts.
why.ko: 계속 불면 풍선은 커지다가 터진다.

gloss.en: The balloon might explode if you keep blowing.
gloss.ko: 계속 불면 풍선이 터질 수도 있어.

lines: This knife is too sharp to cut bread.

why.en: A knife that can't cut has a dull edge.
why.ko: 자르지 못하는 칼 → 날이 무디다.

gloss.en: This knife is too blunt to cut bread.
gloss.ko: 이 칼은 너무 무뎌서 빵을 못 자르겠어.

lines: My old bike is too shiny to ride.

why.en: An old bike you can't ride has been damaged by time.
why.ko: 탈 수 없는 낡은 자전거 → 세월에 상했다.

gloss.en: My old bike is too rusty to ride.
gloss.ko: 내 낡은 자전거는 너무 녹슬어서 탈 수 없어.

lines: It's too quiet to concentrate here.

why.en: What makes it hard to concentrate is sound.
why.ko: 집중을 방해하는 건 소리.

gloss.en: It's too noisy to concentrate here.
gloss.ko: 여기는 너무 시끄러워서 집중이 안 돼.

lines: This photo is too sharp to see clearly.

why.en: You can't see a photo clearly when it is blurred.
why.ko: 사진이 흐릿하면 또렷이 볼 수 없다.

gloss.en: This photo is too fuzzy to see clearly.
gloss.ko: 이 사진은 너무 흐릿해서 잘 안 보여.

lines: I had to mute the TV because it was too quiet.

why.en: You turn the sound off when it is too much.
why.ko: 소리를 끄는 건 소리가 지나칠 때.

gloss.en: I had to mute the TV because it was too loud.
gloss.ko: TV 소리가 너무 커서 음소거해야 했어.

lines: The land was too fertile to grow crops.

why.en: Land where crops can't grow is poor.
why.ko: 작물이 자라지 못하는 땅 → 메마른 땅.

gloss.en: The land was too barren to grow crops.
gloss.ko: 그 땅은 너무 척박해서 농작물을 키울 수 없었어.

lead: Snow is falling and the wind is icy.
lines: You should wear a coat because it’s warm outside.

why.en: Falling snow and an icy wind are the reason you need a coat — not mild weather.
why.ko: 눈이 오고 바람이 차다 → 코트가 필요한 날씨다.

gloss.en: You should wear a coat because it’s cold outside.
gloss.ko: 밖이 추우니까 코트를 입는 게 좋겠어.

lead: I took every book out of it this morning.
lines: This box is full, so you can use it.

why.en: All the books were taken out → nothing is left in the box.
why.ko: 책을 다 꺼냈다 → 상자에 아무것도 없다.

gloss.en: This box is empty, so you can use it.
gloss.ko: 이 상자는 비어 있으니까 써도 돼.

lead: It hung in the sun all afternoon.
lines: The towel is wet now, so you can use it.

why.en: A towel in the sun all afternoon is no longer damp.
why.ko: 오후 내내 햇볕에 걸린 수건 → 축축하지 않다.

gloss.en: The towel is dry now, so you can use it.

lead: You finished every task before anyone else.
lines: I am ashamed of you for working so hard.

why.en: Finishing first after hard work deserves praise, not blame.
why.ko: 열심히 해서 가장 먼저 끝냄 → 비난이 아니라 칭찬할 일.

gloss.en: I am proud of you for working so hard.

lead: I played games all weekend and never opened a book.
lines: I didn't study enough, so I might pass the test.

why.en: No studying → a bad result is likely.
why.ko: 공부를 안 함 → 나쁜 결과가 나올 것.

gloss.en: I didn't study enough, so I might fail the test.
gloss.ko: 공부를 충분히 안 해서 시험에 떨어질지도 몰라.

lead: She wanted the baby to keep sleeping.
lines: She spoke loudly so she wouldn't wake the baby.

why.en: Not waking the baby means keeping your voice low.
why.ko: 아기를 깨우지 않으려면 목소리를 낮춘다.

gloss.en: She spoke softly so she wouldn't wake the baby.
gloss.ko: 그녀는 아기가 깨지 않게 조용히 말했어.

lead: The people at the back keep asking us to repeat everything.
lines: Please speak quietly so everyone can hear.

why.en: People can't hear → you need to speak so every word comes through.
why.ko: 뒤에서 잘 안 들린다 → 말이 또렷이 전달되게 해야 한다.

gloss.en: Please speak clearly so everyone can hear.
gloss.ko: 모두 들을 수 있게 또박또박 말해 주세요.

lead: The train is about to leave the station.
lines: You have to hurry, otherwise you'll be early.

why.en: Hurrying is to avoid missing the time, not to avoid arriving too soon.
why.ko: 서두르는 건 너무 일찍이 아니라 늦지 않으려고.

gloss.en: You have to hurry, otherwise you'll be late.

lead: His best friend had just moved far away.
lines: He smiled even though he was happy.

why.en: A best friend moving away makes you unhappy; 'even though' marks the smile as a contrast.
why.ko: 친한 친구가 멀리 떠남 → 슬프다, even though는 웃음과 반대되는 것.

gloss.en: He smiled even though he was sad.

lead: By the end of the talk, he was smiling and joking.
lines: He was calm initially but relaxed later.

why.en: 'But relaxed later' needs a different feeling at the start.
why.ko: '나중엔 편해졌다'와 대비되는 처음 기분이어야 한다.

gloss.en: He was nervous initially but relaxed later.

lead: She woke up long after her alarm rang.
lines: She was late; therefore, she caught the bus.

why.en: Being late leads to not getting on the bus.
why.ko: 늦었다 → 버스를 타지 못했다.

gloss.en: She was late; therefore, she missed the bus.

lead: The storm lasted all afternoon, and nobody wanted to get wet.
lines: It was raining, so we stayed outside.

why.en: Rain and not wanting to get wet → you stay under a roof.
why.ko: 비가 오고 젖기 싫다 → 지붕 아래에 있는다.

gloss.en: It was raining, so we stayed inside.

lead: I forgot to charge it last night.
lines: The phone is dead, so I can call you.

why.en: A phone with no battery is useless for calling.
why.ko: 배터리가 없는 휴대폰으로는 전화할 수 없다.

gloss.en: The phone is dead, so I can't call you.
gloss.ko: 휴대폰 배터리가 나가서 전화를 못 해.

lead: She always tells the truth, even when it is hard.
lines: You can trust her because she is dishonest.

why.en: Trust comes from telling the truth.
why.ko: 믿음은 진실을 말하는 데서 온다.

gloss.en: You can trust her because she is honest.

lead: She has never eaten meat in her life.
lines: She doesn't eat meat because she's hungry.

why.en: Never eating meat is explained by her diet, not by appetite.
why.ko: 평생 고기를 안 먹은 이유는 식욕이 아니라 식습관.

gloss.en: She doesn't eat meat because she's vegetarian.

lead: I stood alone in a corner all night.
lines: I felt comfortable at the party because I knew no one.

why.en: Knowing nobody and standing alone means you felt out of place.
why.ko: 아는 사람이 없어 혼자 서 있었다 → 어색했다.

gloss.en: I felt awkward at the party because I knew no one.

lead: He was coughing and had no energy.
lines: He stayed home because he felt well.

why.en: Coughing with no energy means he was sick.
why.ko: 기침하고 기운이 없다 → 아팠다.

gloss.en: He stayed home because he felt ill.
gloss.ko: 그는 몸이 안 좋아서 집에 있었어.

lead: My grandmother hates bad manners.
lines: Please ask rudely if you want something.

why.en: Someone who hates bad manners wants you to be polite.
why.ko: 버릇없는 걸 싫어하는 사람 → 예의 있게 말해야 한다.

gloss.en: Please ask nicely if you want something.

lead: She argued for hours and never changed her mind.
lines: She is too modest to admit she was wrong.

why.en: Never changing your mind is what stops you admitting a mistake.
why.ko: 끝까지 생각을 안 바꾸는 성격 → 잘못을 인정하지 못함.

gloss.en: She is too stubborn to admit she was wrong.
gloss.ko: 그녀는 너무 고집이 세서 자기가 틀렸다고 인정하지 않아.

lead: The sky is clear and blue this morning.
lines: It's likely to rain today, but bring an umbrella.

why.en: A clear sky means rain is not expected; 'but' adds the opposite advice.
why.ko: 맑은 하늘 → 비는 안 올 것, but은 그 반대 조언.

gloss.en: It's unlikely to rain today, but bring an umbrella.
gloss.ko: 오늘은 비가 올 것 같지 않지만 우산은 챙겨.

lead: I almost fell asleep in the middle of it.
lines: The movie was mostly exciting, but the ending was good.

why.en: Nearly falling asleep means most of the movie was dull.
why.ko: 중간에 잠들 뻔함 → 영화 대부분이 지루했다.

gloss.en: The movie was mostly boring, but the ending was good.

lead: He can lift heavy boxes with one hand.
lines: He is physically weak because he exercises daily.

why.en: Lifting heavy boxes with one hand shows great strength.
why.ko: 무거운 상자를 한 손으로 듦 → 힘이 세다.

gloss.en: He is physically strong because he exercises daily.

lead: The house was dark and completely silent.
lines: I called out, but everybody was there.

why.en: A dark, silent house means no one answered.
why.ko: 어둡고 조용한 집 → 아무도 대답하지 않았다.

gloss.en: I called out, but nobody was there.

lead: People in the cinema couldn't stop giggling.
lines: The movie was so funny, there was silence everywhere.

why.en: A funny movie and giggling people fill the room with sound.
why.ko: 웃긴 영화, 킥킥대는 사람들 → 웃음소리가 가득.

gloss.en: The movie was so funny, there was laughter everywhere.
gloss.ko: 영화가 너무 웃겨서 여기저기서 웃음이 터졌어.

lead: My friend told the best joke I have ever heard.
lines: It was so funny I literally cried with sadness.

why.en: Crying because something was funny means tears of joy, not grief.
why.ko: 웃겨서 운 것 → 슬퍼서가 아니라 즐거워서 흘린 눈물.

gloss.en: It was so funny I literally cried with laughter.
gloss.ko: 너무 웃겨서 말 그대로 웃다가 울었어.

lead: I have looked in every room for it.
lines: I left my phone someplace, but I can remember where.

why.en: Searching every room means you don't know where it is.
why.ko: 방마다 찾아봄 → 어디 뒀는지 모른다.

gloss.en: I left my phone someplace, but I can't remember where.
gloss.ko: 휴대폰을 어딘가에 뒀는데 어딘지 기억이 안 나.

lead: My fingers were freezing.
lines: I turned off the heater because it was cold.

why.en: Freezing fingers → you want more heat, not less.
why.ko: 손가락이 얼 것 같다 → 열이 더 필요하다.

gloss.en: I turned on the heater because it was cold.

lead: It has rained all morning, and none of us want to get wet.
lines: Let’s stay outdoors because it’s raining.

why.en: Rain and not wanting to get wet → stay under a roof.
why.ko: 비가 오고 젖기 싫다 → 지붕 아래에.

gloss.en: Let’s stay indoors because it’s raining.

lead: He has missed our meetings many times.
lines: He is often late, so he is reliable.

why.en: Often being late and missing meetings means you can't count on him.
why.ko: 자주 늦고 약속을 어김 → 믿고 맡길 수 없다.

gloss.en: He is often late, so he is unreliable.
gloss.ko: 그는 자주 늦어서 믿을 수가 없어.
